overview: Both convert an ore to its oxide by heating, but roasting uses excess air on a sulphide ore, while calcination uses limited/no air on a carbonate or hydroxide ore.
genZNote: Roasting: sulphide ore meets excess air. Calcination: carbonate ore heated with the air kept out.

aspects.label: Type of Ore Used On
aspects.valueB: Typically applied to carbonate or hydroxide ores.

aspects.label: Atmosphere Used
aspects.valueB: Heated in limited air or in its absence.

aspects.label: Gas Released
aspects.valueB: Releases CO₂ (from carbonates) or water vapour (from hydroxides).
